claims.text: Terraform and OpenTofu can use a self-hosted Pulumi Cloud instance as a state backend by setting an environment variable on the API service.
There is a state backend guide located at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/.
The PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable sets the domain that serves the Terraform-compatible API, for example `tf.pulumiapi.acmecorp.com`.
When PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is unset, the Terraform-compatible API is disabled and its routes are not registered.
The DNS record for the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN domain should be pointed at the same host that serves PULUMI_API_DOMAIN.
Using a separate domain for PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN keeps the Terraform-compatible API distinct from the Pulumi API.
A separate domain for the Terraform-compatible API is not required; PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN can be set to the same value as PULUMI_API_DOMAIN to avoid needing a second DNS record.

In the Terraform or OpenTofu configuration, the `terraform login` or `tofu login` command, and the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name, the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN value should be used wherever the state backend guide at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ uses `tf.pulumi.com`.
The state backend guide at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ uses the domain `tf.pulumi.com` as an example.
